name: Nemglan

attributes.attribute: won the throne of Tara after divination
broke a geis to stand between vassals

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Nemglan is the grandfather of Conaire. Conaire traced his descent from Etain, named a goddess or fairy queen. The tale stresses how vital it was for a ruler to obey every sacred vow or geis. Conaire won the throne of Tara after divination, called the bull-sleep, revealed he was the rightful king. Inauguration brought a series of demands. One rule barred him from placing himself between two quarreling vassals. He broke that rule by stepping into a dispute between his brothers. On the way back to Tara he broke other vows. He allowed horsemen dressed in red to overtake him while he rode. He kept Tara to his right as he rode. A terrifying hag came to Da Derga's hostel and demanded that she be let inside. Conaire held to his last geis, that no woman should stay alone with him at night. Cursing him from a magical stance, she left him with a thirst he could not slake even as fire consumed the hostel.

okr.objective: Nemglan is the grandfather of Conaire, whose reign bent to a sacred geis.
